clarifyingQuestions: Would a production format restrict names to a fixed allowlist? This base format preserves any nonempty name.
How would the format escape a literal END line in content?
Should nested opener-looking lines remain content or raise an error in a follow-up?
followUps: Support nested sections explicitly or reject them.
Track line numbers for parser errors.
followUpGuide: Required sections are a post-parse validation pass over the parsed dictionary.

The base parser treats opener-looking lines inside a section as content. To support nesting, define how END closes a stack frame and how child bodies appear in output; a stack alone does not define the representation. Alternatively, explicitly change the grammar to reject nested openers.
Line numbers are easiest if the parser iterates with `enumerate`.
complexityAnalysis: - Explicit state machine: O(n) time for n input characters, assuming expected constant-time dictionary access. Every line is scanned and every completed body joined once. Keep an outside_seen boolean; searching the growing errors list on every outside line could take quadratic time after many duplicates.

- The supplied splitlines version uses O(n) space for split lines, buffered content, stored bodies, names, and errors. It still buffers an unfinished or duplicate body until its closing marker; duplicate bodies are discarded after completion.

- Streaming follow-up can avoid holding all split lines at once, but returning every section and error still requires output space plus the current body and partial line. Memory can fall further only if the API emits completed sections/errors incrementally and defines how it tracks previously seen names.
solutionGuide: Use explicit parser state: current section name and collected lines. Recognize openers only outside sections. Complete a body at exact END, then detect duplicates without overwriting the first completed body. Use a separate boolean for the single outside_text error so reporting stays linear even when duplicates have accumulated.
